I completely agree with this article. Not so much with the headline. I dont' think StackOverflow is going anywhere, but it has a lot of problems as mentioned.
it's frustrating to look up a specific question and 3/4 of the responses are people complaining it wasn't asked 'properly' or people complaining about other answers.

I very much agree on people complaining about other answers. I hate in when questions get marked as duplicates, and the linked "duplicate" is 3-5 years old. New patterns and best practices emerge, new language features are implemented; the programming environment is always changing. The right answer for 3-5 years ago isn't necessarily the right answer for now. Old questions should occasionally be revisited.

I'd argue that old questions shouldn't just occasionally be revisited, but often if you can. My team at work is looking at code we were super proud of 6 months ago and now we are ripping it out to replace it with something much better. Getting different eyes on a problem along with that new tech or new ideas can make us all much better programmers and engineers.

Never had a problem using the site. But I do have nearly 400 answered questions. I really think it down to a few people who monitor specific tags that think they own them. But as a programmer you will need to learn to search for answers before posting your questions. SO is not a place to begin when you want a tutorial, SO is a place to get an answer to specific problems you might face while doing XYZ.

If you want a tutorial there are numerous other sites you can use. However, if you want an answer to a problem you're facing while lets say programming a FPGA, someone on SO probably had the same problem in the past and has already solved it for you. This is why contributing to SO is so important.

Hello, i just wanted to say that i have great respect for you, because i think that our lives are worth just as much as the animals', and i admire your choice to not kill and eat said animals. I am not a vegan myself because i strongly dislike the taste of many vegetables and have difficulties overcoming that.

Note that flavour and texture of food can change drastically based on how you cook it. Boiled brussel sprouts? Disgusting. Cut into two halves and fried until golden brown with a little salt and pepper? Fucking candy. Eggplant, mushrooms, tofu, zucchini: they all depend on how you prepare them in order to be tasty. I mean... raw onions vs onion rings? I'm sure you see my point. ;)

Maybe try out some restaurants that provide options? (but personally, I'd stay away from the raw vegan options as I think fire makes things taste good)

From a health perspective, you pretty much have to eat vegetables because meat and dairy can't supplement all the vitamins and minerals you need.

With that in mind, it is said that flavor changes with time. Try to incorporate more veggies into your diet, you may end up liking it. Like /u/bradbeattie said, it also depends on how you prepare food. Try some new recipes! Veggies are effin' delicious :)
Hi, Sassybanana! There are lots of alternatives out there that aren't vegetables. That said, veggies can be pretty yummy depending on how you fix 'em! :)

Salad (with paprika, tomatoes, ...) is easy to make and always great with the right dressing. What I love to add (to salad, pasta, pretty much everything where it makes sense) is mushrooms. Chamignons, specifically.

The best way to make them (at least from my experience) is to put them in a frying pan (already hot and containing your favourite kind of oil) and add a bit of salt (careful, not too much). When they're almost finished (beige-brownish), add a few squeezes of lemon juice (experiment to find out how much you like) and you're done. Always get fresh mushrooms, the ones in glasses or cans aren't nearly as good.
